content: Denial playbook — CARC 197 (precertification/authorization absent): 1) Check whether a valid authorization is on file for the date of service. 2) If yes, appeal with the authorization attached. 3) If no auth was ever obtained, the amount is a provider write-off under CO — do not balance-bill the patient. Default recommended action: appeal.

Denial playbook — CARC 29 (timely filing expired): 1) Look for proof of timely submission (clearinghouse report, certified mail). 2) If proof exists, appeal within the payer's reconsideration window. 3) If no proof, write off — the practice absorbs it; never bill the patient. Default recommended action: contractual_writeoff.

Denial playbook — CARC 50 (not medically/dentally necessary): 1) Appeal with clinical documentation (narrative, radiographs, perio charting) citing the relevant policy/LCD (often RARC N115). 2) Only shift to the patient if a valid signed waiver/financial agreement predates the service. Default recommended action: appeal.

Denial playbook — CARC 16 / 252 (missing information or documentation required): 1) Read the paired RARC (e.g. M127 missing records) to learn exactly what is needed. 2) Supply the documentation and resubmit/appeal. These are correctable rework denials, not write-offs or patient bills. Default recommended action: appeal.

Denial playbook — CARC 22 / 109 (covered by another payer / not covered by this payer / COB): 1) Identify the correct or secondary payer. 2) Obtain the primary EOB if needed (RARC MA04). 3) Bill the secondary payer; do not bill the patient or write off until the correct payer is exhausted. Default recommended action: bill_secondary.
